football.reason: win and tie handled alike (a tie pays 50/50 on both); differs on postponement past 48h, where Kalshi resolves to a fair price and Polymarket stays open until the game is played

baseball.reason: winner of the game on both; Kalshi resolves a game cancelled or moved more than two days to a fair price, Polymarket waits for the make-up game and pays 50-50 on a cancellation

basketball_hockey.reason: winner including overtime on both; postponement and cancellation are resolved differently (Kalshi fair price, Polymarket 50-50 or open)

soccer.reason: result after 90 minutes plus stoppage time on both, three outcomes (home, draw, away); a cancelled match resolves to a fair price on Kalshi but to No on the team markets and Yes on the draw on Polymarket

tennis.reason: the player who wins or advances once a ball has been played; a walkover before the first ball resolves to a fair price on Kalshi and to the advancing player (or 50-50) on Polymarket

esports.reason: full-match winner on both (map markets excluded); forfeits and postponements past 48h are resolved differently

combat.reason: official winner; draw or no contest pays 50/50 on both; a cancelled or long-postponed bout resolves to a fair price on Kalshi and 50-50 on Polymarket

other_sport.reason: winner of the listed match on both; cancellation and postponement rules differ

election_party.reason: both resolve on the winning nominee’s party; Kalshi on the party of the person sworn in or inaugurated (determined early on a media consensus), Polymarket on the declared winner; they differ only if the winner never takes office or changes party

chamber_control.reason: majority of voting seats, with the Speaker’s party as the fallback on both; Kalshi reads the Speaker on 2027-02-01 if no media consensus
